title: Cana Credit Union
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Lydia wanted to rob the Cana Community Credit Union. She offered Barnabas one-third of the money she stole if Barnabas would drive the getaway van. Barnabas agreed but made Lydia promise not to hurt anyone during the robbery.

Lydia then went to Peter’s outdoor-supply shop. She told Peter that she needed a small handgun for use in a credit-union robbery. Peter said that because Lydia had been foolish enough to reveal her unlawful plan, he would charge extra, and he sold her the handgun at four times its regular price.

During the robbery, Lydia used the handgun to threaten the teller into handing over money. The gun discharged by accident and killed Stephen, a customer. Barnabas drove Lydia away from the credit union.

In addition to Lydia, who could properly be convicted of murder in Stephen’s death at common law?
call: In addition to Lydia, who could properly be convicted of murder in Stephen's death at common law?
rightExplanation:
A is correct.

Silver Key: Read the answer array as a 2×2 liability grid. The choices are not four independent essays. They ask two yes/no questions: (1) Barnabas liable? (2) Peter liable? Once both boxes are “yes,” the residual answer is “both.”

Gold Key: Getaway accomplice + felony murder. Barnabas joined the robbery plan by agreeing to drive the getaway van for a share of the proceeds. A promise not to hurt anyone does not remove him from the robbery. The accidental killing during the robbery is the danger the felony-murder rule attaches to.

Gold Key: Crime-purpose seller with a stake. Peter did more than make an ordinary sale. He was told the gun would be used in the robbery and charged four times the normal price because of that criminal use. That fact supplies the stake/intent signal that makes the sale look like aid to the robbery, not neutral commerce.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text: No answer dies on grammar alone. The array is intentionally clean.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text:
The answer array is a 2×2 matrix:

| Choice | Barnabas liable? | Peter liable? |
| ------ | ---------------- | ------------- |
| A      | Yes              | Yes           |
| B      | No               | No            |
| C      | Yes              | No            |
| D      | No               | Yes           |

c3.label: CALL
c3.text:
Apply two Gold Keys.

* Barnabas box: yes. He joined the robbery and drove the getaway van. Promise-not-to-hurt does not withdraw him.
* Peter box: yes. He knowingly sold the gun for the robbery and charged a crime-based premium.

Residual: A.

studentScript: This is a two-box question. Barnabas: getaway driver, no withdrawal, yes. Peter: knew robbery purpose and charged extra because of it, yes. Yes/yes equals A.

A.lawyer: Barnabas is liable through participation in the robbery and foreseeable felony-murder consequences; Peter is liable because his knowing, crime-premium sale supplies intentional aid.

B.signal: After the Gold Keys, both boxes are yes; this says both are no.
B.lawyer: Both actors can be convicted; this answer denies both liability routes.

C.signal: Correct on Barnabas; misses Peter's crime-purpose sale box.
C.lawyer: Peter's knowledge plus crime-based premium can establish intentional assistance.

D.signal: Correct on Peter; misses Barnabas's continued robbery participation.
D.lawyer: Barnabas remained in the robbery plan; the promise not to hurt anyone did not withdraw him.

goldKeys.statement: A getaway participant in a dangerous felony stays exposed to murder liability for an accidental killing during the felony; a private promise not to hurt anyone does not withdraw him from the felony.
goldKeys.trigger: driver joins robbery for a share, asks for no violence, then drives escape
goldKeys.authority: Cornell Wex felony murder; Justia felony murder; Pinkerton foreseeable co-conspirator acts

goldKeys.statement: A seller crosses from neutral sale to accomplice territory when he knowingly supplies the crime tool and takes a crime-based premium or stake from the illegal use.
goldKeys.trigger: seller is told the item is for the robbery and charges extra because of that purpose
goldKeys.authority: Direct Sales; Backun; Cornell Wex accomplice

silverKeys.statement: When choices are both/neither/only X/only Y, stop reading them as essays. Make two yes/no boxes and resolve each box separately.

remediation.title: Two actors, two boxes
remediation.studentMove: Resolve X first, resolve Y second, then match the combo.
remediation.tinyRule: Do not let one actor you understand hide the other actor.
remediation.trap: Picking C after solving only Barnabas.
